body:
## What was wrong

The check later reminder stopped a turn whenever a memory edit's new text held a future date, even when that date was already in the text the edit replaced. `memory_signal` in `payload/hooks/lib/check-later-signals.py` read only `new_string` (and a Write's `content`) and never looked at what was replaced. On 2026-11-25 a clause added to a MEMORY.md index line that had held 2027-09-15 since September ended the turn with "This turn left a memory note (MEMORY.md) naming Wed Sep 15".

## How it was reproduced

Eleven new cases in `payload/hooks/test-check-later-nudge.sh`, run against the unchanged reader: 56 passed, 11 failed. Every failure was a new behaviour case and every new control passed. The fixtures carry their own timestamp (1:00 PM ET on 2026-11-02) and the suite pins the zone, so no case depends on the real date.

## What changed

- A memory write now counts only a future date its new text names and the text it replaced did not. The replaced text is the Edit's `old_string`, every `old_string` of a MultiEdit taken together, or, for a Write that updated an existing file, the `originalFile` Claude Code records on the tool result line beside the call.
- A MultiEdit applies its edits in order, so a date in a later edit's old text that an earlier edit of the same call wrote does not count as already there (found by the lessons review of the first commit, fixed test first in the second).
- Dates are compared by the day they name, after the same reading that finds them, so `2026-11-05`, `Nov 5th` and `November 5, 2026` are one date. The spelling is not compared, because the signal is about which day a check waits on.
- When a Write has no such record (a new file, a refused call, a result shaped otherwise) every future date counts, as before, so a missing field fails toward firing.
- The reminder names the earliest NEW date, so an edit keeping Nov 4 and adding Nov 9 names Nov 9.
- The cron and promise signals are unchanged. The skill's one line describing the memory signal says what is now true.

## What a session now sees

No CHECK LATER stop for a memory edit that only carries a date along. A memory edit that adds a date still stops the turn, naming that date.

## Tests seen red

Before the fix (56 passed, 11 failed), each now green:

- an Edit whose old and new text share one future date and add none
- an Edit keeping one future date and adding a second names only the new one
- the same date in two forms, ISO to month name and month name with year to ISO
- a replace_all Edit carrying its date along
- a MultiEdit carrying its date along, and one moving a date between lines in one call
- a MultiEdit adding a date names only that date
- a date written twice before and once after
- a Write updating a memory whose earlier content held the same date, and one adding a date names only the new one

Then, before the second commit (67 passed, 1 failed): a MultiEdit whose later edit reworks a date its earlier edit added still names that date.

Controls that passed before and after: an Edit adding a date, a replace_all Edit adding a date, a Write creating a memory, a Write with no record of its earlier content.

## The measurement

Read on 2026-11-26 from this Mac's transcripts for the 31 days before it: 9 distinct reminders named a memory note (6 further copies sit in resumed or forked session files and were counted once). In 1 of the 9 the named date was already in the replaced text: the Sep 15 case above. In 5 the Edit added the date, and in 3 a Write named it with no record of the earlier content. So this fix would have silenced 1 of 9.

All 9 of those tool calls were denied by the permission layer before they ran (the denying list includes the ask-before-saving mod). That is a separate question, recorded as a side finding rather than changed here.

## Suites

- `payload/hooks/test-check-later-nudge.sh`: 68 passed, 0 failed
- `tests/test-sleep-silence.sh`: 144 passed, 0 failed
- `payload/hooks/test-per-prompt-hook-cost.sh`: 32 passed, 0 failed
- `payload/hooks/test-skill-integrity.sh`: 41 passed, 0 failed

Each run alone in the worktree on the final tree. The full `run-all-tests.sh` was not run. The push gate's lessons check flagged L13 and L71 (background work and watchdogs); neither applies, since this change adds no scheduled or background work.

## What is not established

- The Write comparison rests on `originalFile` being present on an update's result line. It was on 5 of 5 memory Write updates in 31 days on this Mac; the work MacBook was not measured.
- An Edit is compared with its own `old_string` only, as the issue asks. A date retyped into a new line while it already sits elsewhere in the file still fires.
- Whether the 8 other reminders were wanted. Each named a date its write added, but each write was denied before it ran.

## For Dan

The open question was whether a Write replacing a whole memory file should be compared with the file's earlier content. It can be, honestly and cheaply: by the time the Stop hook runs the disk already holds the new file, but the tool result line Claude Code writes beside a Write records `type` and, for an update, the whole earlier file as `originalFile`. No search for an earlier Read is needed. This is built and tested here. Over 31 days on this Mac there were 63 memory Write creates and 5 updates, all 5 with the earlier content recorded, and none of the 3 Write reminders in that window had it, because each Write was denied before it ran.

## Area check

Area check: scratchpad probe_shapes.py run under a perl alarm: proceed, a read only probe of transcripts printing key names and counts, writing no file.
Area check: scratchpad probe_shapes2.py run under a perl alarm: proceed, the same read only probe with one more breakdown, writing no file.

Closes #3645
title: Stop the check later reminder firing on a date a memory edit only carries along

body:
## What was wrong

When a pull request's checks reused an earlier green run of the same tree, the merge helper followed that run to its "Not tested by the checks" notice and used its records to choose which suites to run before merging. Its log, though, said only "its list of what it did not test is used" and named none of the parts. The helper printed only the notices on the head's own checks, and a reused run has none. So for that kind of head, the fourth line of "What done looks like" (the merge log names the unmeasured parts before it merges) was not true.

Reproduced in test-merge-when-ready-untested.sh: two new checks on the existing reused run case failed first (red.txt), with the log holding no "Not tested by the checks" line and no part.

## What was already true, and how I know

Read on 2026-11-26 against main at 9e67f09.

- A step summary listing each suite with an untested part and its reason: true for every full run. The `suite` job's step "Say which parts the checks did not test" writes it with tools/ci-unmeasured-summary.sh. On run 45758878769 that step succeeded and its notice reads "75 parts in 54 suites were not tested ... and 51 more parts, listed in the run's summary". GitHub offers no command or API that returns a job's summary, so its content is proved by tools/test-ci-unmeasured-summary.sh rather than read off the run.
- Derived from what the suites print: true. run-all-tests.sh reads each `SUITE-PART-UNMEASURED` line and writes the record the tool reads; the tool names no suite. That is the one shared shape: 111 suite files use it, none prints another wording, and run-all-tests.sh fails a suite that does.
- More untested than main, shown without opening a log: true, and now seen on a real run. Run 45758878769 carries the annotation "Not tested by the checks and more than on main".
- The merge log naming the parts: true for a head with its own notice; built here for a head whose checks reused a run.

#3438 (fix/3312-notice-cut-at-4096) merged on 2026-11-22, so the notice is held under GitHub's length limit and ends with how many more parts there are.

## What changed

- payload/hooks/lib/merge-when-ready.sh: say_untested also prints the notice of the run the checks reused, naming that run, through one function shared with the head's own notices. It is keyed to the head, so a notice followed for an earlier head is never printed for a later one. The change only reports. What runs or refuses before a merge is unchanged.
- payload/hooks/test-merge-when-ready-untested.sh: two checks on the reused run case.
- README.md: the passage on the merge helper's reading says what is now true.

## Tests

Seen red first: the two new checks (red.txt), 245 passed and 2 failed before the change; 247 passed and 0 failed after.

Suites run, each alone, on the personal MacBook on 2026-11-26, every one with 0 failed: test-merge-when-ready-untested.sh 247 passed, test-merge-when-ready.sh 476, test-merge-when-ready-heads.sh 292, test-merge-when-ready-line.sh 134, test-merge-when-ready-turn.sh 204, test-merge-when-ready-bypass.sh 377, tools/test-ci-unmeasured-summary.sh 32.

## What is not established

- The new log lines have been seen only against the suite's stand in GitHub. A real merge whose checks reused an earlier run is rare: none of the newest 60 completed pull request runs of tests.yml reused one (2026-11-26).
- A main baseline that trails main's tip. Main's record of what it left untested is saved only by a full run on main, and a push to main that reuses the pull request's run saves none. On run 45758878769 a suite main had gained one minute earlier (test-agent-leftovers.sh, from #3623) was reported as more untested than main, because the baseline came from a run before #3623. That is one sample, and it is recorded for a separate issue, not fixed here.

## For Dan

- Item 3 on the issue is still yours: whether a reused run's checks should carry the list of the run they reuse. Today its summary links that run and says the list is on that run's page. Recommendation: keep the link. Pull request runs that reuse are rare (0 of the newest 60), the merge log now names the parts either way, and copying the list would need the `suite` job to read the Actions API, which it cannot do today.
- Until that is settled, the first line of "What done looks like" is not met for a reused run, so this is Part of #3312, not Closes.

Part of #3312
title: Name a reused run's untested suite parts in the merge helper's log

body:
## What was wrong

Two parts of the sync suite failed on a busy Mac with nothing wrong in what they test.

The lesson number checks (#1148) start five sessions asking for a number at once. Each ask waits its turn for a small lock, and the wait gave up ten seconds after the ask started, however many asks were ahead of it. On a busy Mac each ask holds the lock for one to four seconds, so the last ones in the queue gave up and said "another ask has held the lock for less than a minute", which was not true of any one of them. That is a real fault in the lock, not only in the test: five real sessions asking at once on a busy Mac would have been turned away the same way. No session was ever given a number twice.

The suite stop checks (#464) held a whole send or pull to 20 seconds of wall clock. The thing they guard against is a send that waits out a stuck suite's 40 second sleep. On a busy Mac a send that stopped the suite correctly still took longer than 20 seconds, because the send also does its own repository work.

## How it was reproduced

All on the personal MacBook on 2026-11-25, inside `tools/load-window.sh`.

- Lesson numbers: the section's own fixture, five asks at once, 8 rounds with 48 busy workers (load 83 to 139). 6 of the 8 rounds lost one to four asks, every one at the lock's ten second limit. The section itself, run 5 times at a lighter load (82 to 158), passed each time.
- Suite stop: the unchanged section with 64 busy workers. The send check failed at 45.4 seconds against its 20 second bound, the failure the issue saw at 24.8 seconds.

## What changed

- The lock (`hooks/lib/pid-lock.sh`, shared by lesson numbers, the hold record and the scanners gate) now gives up only when one holder has kept it past the limit. The wait starts again each time the lock changes hands, so a moving queue is waited for. A test can set the lock's clock (`PID_LOCK_TEST_CLOCK`), and a clock that prints no number makes the wait give up and say so.
- The five session race checks run on a lock clock that stands still, so they judge only what the asks did. Three new checks drive the limit on a clock the test moves: a lock passed from holder to holder is waited for and taken, one holder keeping it is still refused, and a bad clock gives up by name.
- The five 20 second checks now judge what the stop did: the stuck suite's sleeps write down how they ended, and a sleep that ran its full 40 seconds means the run waited it out. The fixture clock stands still between stages, so no stage can end by running out of time. If the Mac reached a stage only after its sleep had already ended on its own, the check reports itself as not measured, in the line the runner counts, never as a pass or a failure.
- README says the lock waits for one holder, not the whole queue. Two comments in `claude-sync` say the same.

## Tests seen red

- Against the old lock library: the hand off check and the bad clock check fail, the control passes.
- Against a `claude-sync` whose stop is a signal and then a plain wait (the original #464 fault): all five new stop checks fail, the other 68 checks pass.

## Green, and the counts

- First half alone: 1891 passed, 0 failed, 480 seconds (before: 1888, 453 seconds in #3680). The 3 added checks are the new lock checks.
- Second half alone: 1997 passed, 0 failed, 531 seconds (before: 1995 checks). The 2 added checks come from splitting two checks that mixed a time bound with "nothing left running"; both halves are still checked.
- Lesson number section alone: 68 checks became 71, 15 seconds before and 14 after. Suite stop section alone: 71 became 73, 26 seconds before and 25 to 29 after.
- Under load windows on the branch: the five asks at once, 8 rounds at load 54 to 113, gave all 40 asks a number with none repeated, the last ask of a round taking up to 37 seconds. Each section also finished once under load (load 116 and 139) and passed every check. Most other windows were cut short by other sessions' merges and reviews.
- The scanners gate suite, which tests the same lock library: 232 passed, 0 failed, 378 seconds.
- The lessons check on push flagged a fixed wait in the suite. That does not apply: the lines it matches start four `sleep 300` processes that stand in as live lock holders and are stopped by name straight after.

## Not verified

- A full run of either half inside a load window: a window lasts at most 180 seconds and each half takes many minutes, so only the two sections ran under load. Other sessions' merges and reviews cut most windows short; the runs that finished under load are listed above.
- A stop check can still fail if the Mac sees the deadline in time but then takes more than 40 seconds to stop the suite. That is the fault's own sign and is twice the old bound, measured from the stuck point rather than from the start of the send.

## For Dan

Nothing needs you. The lock now waits for each holder in turn, which applies to the hold record and the scanners gate too. The one place that wanted a short wait, `claude-sync status` clearing old holds, still gives up after one second when one run keeps the lock; it waits longer only while several runs change the hold record one after another.

Area check: tests/test-claude-sync.sh: proceed, the change fixes existing checks in place inside two existing sections and adds no section; the file's size is tracked in #3680.
Area check: the worktree (test runs): proceed, each held command only ran test sections or the suite, writing nothing in the worktree and its output to the session scratchpad.

Closes #3683
title: Wait for each lock holder in turn, and judge the suite stop by what it stopped (#3683)

body:
## What was wrong

Every pull writes grep, rg, egrep, fgrep, cat, head and tail into rtk's excluded list, but rtk 0.31.0 still rewrites a grep that has something in front of it. On 2026-11-25 on the personal MacBook, `rtk rewrite` was asked about 357 commands (7 commands, 17 prefixes, 3 argument sets each), and 96 were rewritten:

- grep and rg behind `FOO=1`, `VAR=1 OTHER=2`, `env`, `env FOO=1` and `sudo` all became the same prefix followed by `rtk grep` (rg lands on `rtk grep` too), in all 3 argument sets.
- cat, head and tail behind the same five prefixes became `rtk read`, which the hook already refuses.
- `git status && <command>` had only its git part rewritten.

Not rewritten in any argument set: `time`, `nice`, `nice -n 5`, `command`, `timeout 5`, `xargs`, a full path `/usr/bin/grep`, and grep after `cd /tmp &&`, `true;` or a pipe. egrep and fgrep were never rewritten behind any prefix.

`rtk grep -h` prints rtk's help and exits 0. In 3 of 3 runs it printed 19 help lines and no matches, where `/usr/bin/grep -h` on the same files printed both matching lines. So a prefixed grep lost its matches and still reported success.

## What the two commits do

1. The failing tests (e853170). test-rtk-rewrite.sh expects the hook to refuse any rewrite that runs rtk with a subcommand on rtk's own excluded list. It covers the measured shapes, rg, compound commands, and a list printed on one line. Its controls are: the list installed with git status kept; grep as an argument kept; an empty list keeping `rtk grep`, as Dan decided in #1419 for a grep standing alone; and the same name under another table not counting. An end to end check writes payload/rtk-exclude-commands.txt into a throwaway HOME's rtk config and runs the measured shapes through the real rtk and the real hook. The stub rtk now answers `config`.
2. The fix (80916dd). The hook reads the excluded list once from `rtk config`, which is the copy of payload/rtk-exclude-commands.txt each pull writes into rtk's config. It then refuses inside rtk_refused_destination, beside the `rtk read` refusal. There is one list, and the hook adds no copy of it. This commit also corrects one control (below) and re-records .rtk-hook.sha256.

## Tests seen red, and where green comes from

Red was seen in Dan's own run of the suite at e853170 on 2026-11-25: 230 passed, 16 failed. Fifteen of the failures were the new refusal cases and the checks against the real rtk, each naming the rewrite it got.

The sixteenth was a control that failed for a reason of its own: "nor does grep as an argument of another subcommand refuse". Its rewrite was `rtk git log --grep x`, and the hook already refuses every `rtk git log` (#3469), so that control could never pass, with or without the fix. Commit 2 changes it to `rtk ls grep`, which puts grep in the argument slot the scan reads and which nothing else refuses. It now passes only because the new refusal keys on the subcommand alone.

The suite cannot be run in a session on the personal MacBook (claude-config#3640), so the green run is CI's run on this pull request. Checked by hand on 2026-11-25, one run each: `bash -n` on both files, and the hook's own list reader cut from the file and applied to real `rtk config` output and real `rtk rewrite` answers. The installed list read as grep rg egrep fgrep cat head tail. The measured shapes were refused, and so was cd && FOO=1 grep. git status and ls -la were kept. An empty list, a failing `rtk config` and a list under another table each refused nothing.

## A comment reworded for the Slack drafts gate

The Slack drafts gate refused a local run of the suite because it could not read one comment in rtk-rewrite.sh. The comment was reworded with no code changed, and .rtk-hook.sha256 was re-recorded. claude-config#3640 stays open for the gate itself. After that, the gate refused the suite again, this time for the existing #1428 curl check, so the suite still runs only in CI.

Old:

    # A `)` that closes nothing it can name (a case pattern, a stray) is not guessed at.

New:

    # A closing parenthesis that closes nothing it can name, a case pattern or a stray one, is not guessed at.

## What a session now sees

A prefixed grep or rg runs exactly as written, with grep's own output and exit code. Every other rewrite is unchanged.

## Not established

- The work MacBook was not measured. Its list comes from the same file, installed by pull.
- A Mac whose rtk config has no list gets no extra refusal from this change. There rtk rewrites even a bare grep, as it does today, and `claude-sync status` reports that Mac's list as different.
- If rg were taken off the list but grep kept, `FOO=1 rg` would still be refused, since it lands on `rtk grep`. The reverse case would let it through.
- The suite has not been seen green on any Mac yet. That is CI's run.
- Reading the list costs one more `rtk config` call, made only when rtk has offered a rewrite. Its time was not measured.

## After it merges

Run `claude-sync pull` on each Mac. It installs the hook, and its ensure_rtk_baseline step re-derives hooks/.rtk-hook.sha256 from the installed hook, so rtk keeps running. Nothing else is needed.

## For Dan

Nothing to decide. At e853170 the lessons review raised two findings, both saying the hook did not yet do what the new tests expect, which is what that commit held. Its review at 80916dd raised none.

Area check: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-danielhankins-wright-Non-icloudDocuments-Apps-claude-config/3760fc0b-01aa-41f1-ae21-bf57f18f0520/scratchpad/3639/probe.tsv: proceed, The command only runs a read only probe of rtk rewrite and writes its output to a file in this session's scratchpad, outside the repository, so it touches no file in danwright32/claude-config.
Area check: payload/hooks/rtk-rewrite.sh: proceed, This edit rewords one existing comment line in place and adds no line, and the #3639 fix that follows adds one refusal inside the existing rtk_refused_destination function plus a short read of rtk's list, rather than a new section or mechanism, so it does not add to the size problem #3548 tracks.
Area check: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-danielhankins-wright-Non-icloudDocuments-Apps-claude-config/3760fc0b-01aa-41f1-ae21-bf57f18f0520/scratchpad/3639/check-reader.sh: proceed, The command runs a read only check script from the scratchpad that only reads the hook file and asks rtk for its config and rewrites, printing to the terminal, so it writes no file in danwright32/claude-config.

Closes #3639
title: Stop the rtk hook rewriting a prefixed grep into rtk grep (#3639)
